analyst_view.overall: Sunderland are bottom with 5 points from 9 games and only 7 league goals, and Régis Le Bris is under pressure after a 3-1 loss at Coventry and a 2-0 home defeat to Dinamo Zagreb on Thursday, when fans booed at half-time and full-time. They also have only three days' rest against Chelsea's full week, and centre-backs Ballard and Alderete (suspended) are missing, though Le Bris says Mukiele should be available. Xabi Alonso's Chelsea are 4th; João Pedro, Lacroix, Reece James and Gittens are out, while Caicedo ('a discomfort more than the calf') and Emiliano Martínez face late fitness checks.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Sunderland have scored 7 in 9 league games and Le Bris has admitted his side lack quality in front of goal. Chelsea are without their main striker João Pedro and may have to rely on Palmer as a false nine, so a tight, low-scoring game looks more likely than a shootout.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners. Chelsea should have most of the ball and Sunderland will try to lift a nervous home crowd, but nothing in the news points clearly away from the model.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards. A bottom-placed home side with a manager under pressure and a restless crowd makes for a scrappy, high-stakes game. Sunderland are also missing two centre-backs, which can lead to more desperate tackling, and Jarred Gillett referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.2 shots. Sunderland's tired legs after Thursday and Chelsea's missing striker roughly cancel out against Chelsea's extra rest and expected dominance of the ball, so we stay with the model.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. Sunderland have struggled to turn possession into clear chances, and Chelsea's attack loses its focal point without João Pedro. We expect slightly fewer clean efforts than the model.
